profile.reading: Spectrum Charlotte National Data Center is a Charter Communications facility, operating under the Spectrum consumer brand, in Charlotte, North Carolina. A dedicated data center industry aggregator listing for this exact named facility, Baxtel, gives an address of 7910 Crescent Executive Drive, Charlotte, North Carolina, differing from this row's earlier reverse geocoded approximation of 8730 Green Ridge Drive. Given the aggregator's exact name match to this facility, the Baxtel sourced address is treated as the more reliable of the two and applied here in place of the earlier estimate. The same Baxtel listing describes an $82 million National Data Center comprising a 178,000 square foot primary data center building with four 12,000 square foot data halls, plus a separate four story, 103,500 square foot administrative office building, together housing 1,600 equipment racks. Initial power deployment includes four 500 kilowatt generators, with an ultimate design specification of eight 2,500 kilowatt generators at full build out, and both buildings pursued LEED Silver certification. Originally built by Time Warner Cable, the facility passed to Charter Communications when Charter absorbed Time Warner Cable in a 2016 merger; the company now operates its residential cable, internet, and phone services under the Spectrum consumer brand. Charter and Spectrum branded data centers supporting these operations, including this facility, are not typically marketed as public colocation facilities, unlike wholesale or retail colocation operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, though this specific National Data Center appears to have received unusually detailed public construction and capacity disclosure relative to Charter's other facilities, likely due to public construction project reporting and Time Warner Cable's own original press activity around the buildout. This registry also tracks a separate Centennial, Colorado National Data Center West campus under the same Charter Communications operator, suggesting the company built at least two similarly named National Data Center facilities during the Time Warner Cable era to support its combined video, internet, voice, and billing operations nationally.

This facility has no published power specification, published rack or accelerator count, cooling capacity, or electrical certifications on record. Without these figures, no assessment of its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling is possible from available sources.

The Spectrum Charlotte National Data Center is ranked sixth among North Carolina facilities with published capacity data, though that ranking reflects the absence of published specifications rather than confirmed scale. North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities, of which only five have disclosed power capacity to this site, totaling 50.3 megawatts across the state. This facility contributes zero to that published total.

Charter Communications operates this facility as part of its cable and internet business, not as a marketed hyperscale property with disclosed specifications. No operator specification page, aggregator listing, or public documentation for this specific address has been located that states its power capacity, IT load, or grid interconnection details. Until such specifications are published, this campus cannot be evaluated as a constraint on AI infrastructure.
